cur:catacombs-dogmatic-sarcophagus.summary: Two crowded registers flank a shell medallion with the portraits of a married couple. Above, the creation of Eve and Christ with Adam and Eve are followed by Christ's miracles at Cana, of the loaves and of Lazarus; below, the Magi adore the Child on Mary's lap, Christ heals the blind man and foretells Peter's denial. The sarcophagus sets the whole story of salvation, from creation to resurrection, around the hope of the dead couple.
facts: It was found in the 19th century during rebuilding at San Paolo fuori le Mura and is catalogued as Vatican 104.
Its name comes from the scene of three similar figures creating Eve, read as an allusion to the Trinity and the doctrine of the Council of Nicaea (325).
Wikipedia notes stylistic links with the reliefs added to the Arch of Constantine (315), suggesting a related workshop.
